In mathematics, a '''Suslin algebra''' is a [[Boolean algebra (structure)|Boolean algebra]] that is [[complete Boolean algebra|complete]], [[Atom (order theory)|atomless]], countably [[Distributive property|distributive]], and satisfies the [[countable chain condition]]. They are named after [[Mikhail Yakovlevich Suslin]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Jech|first=Thomas|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GHjmCAAAQBAJ&dq=Suslin+algebra&pg=PA274|title=Set Theory|date=2013-06-29|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3-662-22400-7|language=en}}</ref>

The existence of Suslin algebras is independent of the axioms of [[ZFC]], and is equivalent to the existence of [[Suslin tree]]s or [[Suslin line]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The mathematics of Andrei Suslin|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/2020-57-01/S0273-0979-2019-01680-2/viewer/|access-date=2021-08-08|website=www.ams.org|date=6 July 2019 |language=en}}</ref>
